Name: Codex Usage Meter Desk Display
Short description: The Codex Usage Meter is a tiny desk display that shows your OpenAI Codex 5-hour and weekly limits at a glance. Set up with just your phone. Also works with Claude Code.
Description:
The Codex Usage Meter from Encinitas 3D puts your OpenAI Codex limits on your desk. If you live in Codex, you know the question: how much of my 5-hour limit is left before this task finishes? codeMeter answers it without opening a terminal. It's a small, always-on color display that shows your 5-hour limit and your weekly limit as big percentages with segmented bars, reset countdowns, and amber and red warnings when you're running ahead of the clock. It runs on its own over Wi-Fi. No laptop, no app, no command line, nothing to copy and paste. Set it up once with your phone and it quietly keeps you honest.

How the Codex Usage Meter sets up (about 5 minutes)

  1. Plug it in. Any USB-C charger or port. The screen shows STEP 1 with a QR code.
  2. Join its Wi-Fi. On your phone, join codeMeter-XXXXXX (the name is on the screen, or scan the QR). A setup page opens; if not, visit http://192.168.4.1.
  3. Pick OpenAI Codex. Tap Setup Device. Under "Which do you use?" tap OpenAI Codex, choose your home Wi-Fi, enter its password, and Save.
  4. Sign in with the code. codeMeter restarts and shows a blue SIGN IN screen with a QR code and a short code like ABC1-2DEFG. On your phone, open auth.openai.com/codex/device (or scan the QR), sign in to ChatGPT, and type the code.
  5. Done. The screen says "You're all set" and your usage appears within seconds.

The code is valid for 15 minutes. If it expires, press button B for a new one. A printed quick-start card is in the box.

What to expect

  • Setup: about 5 minutes, entirely on your phone.
  • The screen: "5h limit" and "Weekly limit" percentages, segmented bars, a thin elapsed-time marker, reset time plus countdown, and amber/red pace warnings. Codex devices use a blue >_ codex theme, so they're easy to tell apart from an orange Claude one.
  • Refresh: every 60 seconds. Firmware updates install themselves over Wi-Fi (it checks every 6 hours).
  • If the login lapses: the device renews its ChatGPT sign-in on its own (about every 10 days). If that ever fails, the screen says "Codex login expired". Hold button B about 7 seconds and sign in again on the device. Your Wi-Fi is kept.

What the Codex Usage Meter shows

  • 5h limit and Weekly limit, as big readable percentages.
  • A segmented bar for each, with a thin elapsed-time marker so you can see if you're spending faster than the window is passing.
  • Pace warnings: the bar stays blue; the percentage, the card outline and corner dot, and the time line turn amber when you're running ahead and red when you're clearly overspending.
  • Reset countdowns: "resets 4:35pm in 2h 14m", "resets Thu 9am in 4d 7h".
  • A Status screen (hold button A) with Wi-Fi, signal, IP, uptime, and "Service: Codex (plus)".

What's in the box

  • codeMeter: an M5Stack Core (ESP32) with a 320×240 color LCD and three buttons, pre-flashed and ready.
  • A 3D-printed desk stand, printed to order here in Encinitas, CA.
  • A USB-C cable.
  • A printed quick-start card for the Codex setup.
  • Optional Standard or All Day battery for cord-free placement (choose Battery above).

Switching between Codex and Claude

One firmware supports both. To switch, hold button C for about 7 seconds (a red RESET screen appears at 5 seconds; keep holding) to wipe the device, set it up again, and pick the other service. No reflashing.

Privacy & security (we're upfront about this)

  • Your ChatGPT sign-in is stored on the device only. There's no Encinitas 3D server and no account with us.
  • The device connects directly to OpenAI (or Anthropic if you pick Claude) over encrypted connections, plus GitHub for firmware updates, internet time servers, and ip-api.com for a timezone lookup. That's the complete list.
  • You stay in control: to cut off a lost device, sign it out from your ChatGPT account's security settings (for example "Log out of all devices"). Before lending or reselling, wipe it by holding button C for about 7 seconds.
